summary: Recovered `/srv/archive` online. Utilization fell from 100% to 7%, `archiveapp` can write successfully, existing archive data is intact, and node1 passed the mandatory reboot recovery check.
actions_performed: Identified `/srv/archive/.telemetry-cache/collector-debug.capture` (690,073,600 bytes) as the unexpected consumer.
Moved the inactive capture to root-only quarantine at `/var/tmp/archive-recovery-quarantine/collector-debug.capture` rather than deleting it.
Verified a 1 MiB fsynced write as `archiveapp` and removed the probe.
Confirmed the archive manifest and quarantined capture retained their original SHA-256 hashes.
Safely rebooted node1 once and verified filesystem, services, data, and write capability after recovery.

evidence.summary: The archive XFS filesystem was 100% full; the 690,073,600-byte root-owned collector debug capture accounted for virtually all used space, while archiveapp writes failed with ENOSPC.
The capture was moved outside the archive filesystem. Utilization became 7% with 659 MiB available and remained 7% after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Ensure `archiveapp` can write to the incoming directory
evidence.summary: The initial write failed with ENOSPC; subsequent 1 MiB fsynced writes succeeded before and after reboot with files owned by archiveapp:archiveapp.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the filesystem and existing archive data
evidence.summary: The original manifest hash remained c27a3936… and the capture hash remained 6ca8b133… after being quarantined and after reboot; the XFS archive mount recovered read-write.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 8f258838-e1de-494d-9d99-e5113b2865db; systemd acknowledged the delayed reboot, the node disconnected, and returned with boot ID 8b56ee0d-ac8c-4488-b5a0-a2a9b062d22b. System state, required services, archive mount, hashes, capacity, and archiveapp writes all recovered.
